_comment: Act V (#270 beats 2-3): Pisces at the sealed rune-door. THE DOOR NEVER SPEAKS -- every option this beat needs lives on him. Beat 2's OR-parity is the `the_appetite` arm: #270 wants EITHER read to unlock beat 3, but only one counter can gate an option, so the rune-read player gets the ward fact from Pisces himself (the third producer of read_the_feeding_ward) and lands on the same choice.

at_the_door.speaker: Pisces
at_the_door.text: Do not touch it yet. I have waited a month to stand in front of this. Kindly permit me the first reading, which I cannot take with your hand across the lines.

text_variants.text: The same hand. I have now said so four times and it has not once stopped being remarkable. Ask me what it is for. Go on, ask.
A feeding ward. Under a city. Cut by whoever cut the frame you eat breakfast beside. I need a moment, and then I need a decision, and I would rather it were yours.

text_variants._comment: One arm per outcome, appended after the reading arms so last-match-wins leaves him standing in the ending the player chose. seal_kept_fed sits LAST on purpose: it is the only outcome another path can be layered on top of (a player who opened the seal and then walked back out of the vault without touching the anchor can still fund the keeper), and the fed line is the true state in that case. #440 narrowed how that state is REACHED -- the warden is down before seal_opened can bank, so 'opened it and lost the fight' is gone -- but the layering itself is untouched.
text_variants.text: It is open, and it is quiet, and I have been standing in the doorway for an hour deciding whether that is a relief. Ceria would already be inside. I am still in the doorway.
Your cut is holding. I have checked it eleven times. The twelfth check is scheduled for after supper.
There is a Watch keeper now, with a ledger line to his name, and the ward goes on eating on his schedule. I am going to write it up, and I already know the paper will be insufferable.

options._comment: The OR-bridge: a player who only matched the hand (bare interact or [Observe]) hears the appetite from the man himself. Hidden once the fact is held, by whichever route landed it.
options.text: What is it for, then?

options._comment: #440 THE CHOKEPOINT ROW. Accomplishment gates HIDE, so without this row a player who has read the ward and not yet dealt with the alcove would find the hub silently one row short and no reason given. It is the signpost for the gate on the row below, and it retires the moment the warden is down.
options.text: Something in that alcove is watching us.

options._comment: 2026-07-26 Act V beat 3, THE CHOICE. One entry, three forks inside, so the decision is made in one place and reads as a decision. Gated on the ward fact (never on which Skill read it) and hidden once resolved. #440: seal_warden_downed JOINS that gate (one accomplishment dict, ANDed by _meets_progress) -- the warden wakes on the reading and stands between the reader and every ending, so all three forks are now POST-FIGHT resolutions. The counter can never precede read_the_feeding_ward (it is the encounter's own arming gate), so the compound cannot reorder the beats.
options.text: So what do we do about a door that eats?
Take your moment.

the_watcher._comment: #440. The chokepoint's one node: it names the wall, says why it is there, and sends the player at it. It banks NOTHING -- the only producer of seal_warden_downed is the alcove's own on_victory, so no conversation can talk past the fight. Both exits are ungated (softlock guard) and neither ends the arc.
the_watcher.speaker: Pisces
the_watcher.text: I know. It woke the moment I said out loud what this ward has been doing, which I intend to take as a compliment. It belongs to the door, not to the dungeon: three centuries in a niche with the dust settling on it, left here against exactly one thing happening, and it has just happened. Whatever we decide about the seal, we decide it past that. Deal with it and I will hold the reading open while you do.

options.text: Then it goes down first.
One thing at a time. Where were we?

the_choice._comment: THREE REAL-COST PATHS (#270 beat 3), each with its own producer: FIGHT banks seal_opened here and resolves in the vault beyond the warden; TALK points at Olesm, whose arm carries the Skill-or-gold cost and banks seal_kept_fed + seal_resolved; SKILL closes it here, but only for a player holding BOTH a warding Skill and a piece of warded ruin-stone, whichever arm they take being CONSUMED.
the_choice.speaker: Pisces
the_choice.text: We open it and see what three centuries of feeding produced. Or we leave it fed and make that somebody's paid duty, which is dull, and correct, and I resent both qualities. Or — if your hands are equal to it, which remains unproven — you re-cut the ward yourself and it holds another age without a keeper. I dislike most of these. I will be copying the outer lines while you decide.

options.text: We open it.
It stays fed. The Watch can pay for it.

options._comment: SKILL fork, visible-locked (the witch pattern). TWO entry arms because #270 names both a warding Skill and a reading one and `requires` cannot compound {skill, item} -- the Skill gate opens the pitch and the ITEM gate closes it one node down. That is the shipped multi-node persuade shape, not a gate stacked on a gate.
options.text: [Hedge Remedy] I can re-cut it. Properly.
[Detect Magic] I can re-cut it. I have read enough of these now.
Not yet. Let me think.

fork_open._comment: seal_opened is banked on the OPTION, not here, so the door opens the instant the decision is made. #440 RE-CHOREOGRAPHED: the warden no longer arms here (it armed at the reading and is already down, or this row would not have rendered), so the old line's 'Expect a guardian' promised a fight the player has just finished. He still does not come through: the ward re-seals the moment nobody holds the reading open, which is why the harness cell stays SOLO.
fork_open.speaker: Pisces
fork_open.text: Then stand clear of it. The reading has to stay open while the seal comes apart, which means I am occupied and you are on your own for whatever else objects to this. The alcove was the first answer to that question. I would not assume it was the only one.

options.text: Understood.

fork_fed.speaker: Pisces
fork_fed.text: Sensible. Deeply unsatisfying. It will need a real keeper, though, and a real ledger line, or it lapses in a decade and we are back here with worse knees. Olesm keeps the Watch's dread and the Watch's paperwork in the same drawer. Go and tell him what is eating under his city. Spare no detail.

options.text: I'll go and see him at the Guild.
Back up a moment.

fork_reward._comment: The item gate closes the fork. `requires {item}` renders VISIBLE-LOCKED with its own reason string, NOT hidden -- dialogue.gd hides only accomplishment-shaped gates (_progress_gated) -- so a player holding neither piece sees both arms and what each wants. TWO close arms, not one: guardian_ward_fragment drops only from ruin_guardian, the FIGHT breach of the dig's pedestal, and Hedault's trade consumes it, so a plates-or-wardwork player had no route to seal_rewarded at all. construct_core_shard is the MAIN-LINE drop (vault_boss_slot, chance 1.0, no other sink), so the second arm is the universal one. Each arm consumes its own item, so the real cost is preserved on both.
fork_reward.speaker: Pisces
fork_reward.text: You would need warded stone to cut into — the same age, the same craft, already carrying a working of its own. Ruin-stone: the pedestal guardian out at the ruin was made of it, and so is the core the vault construct was carrying when it came apart. If you kept either piece, this becomes a long afternoon and a permanent answer.

options.text: I kept the guardian's fragment. Cut it from that.
I kept the construct's core shard. Cut it from that.
Then it'll have to be another way.

fork_reward_done.speaker: Pisces
fork_reward_done.text: There. The pour runs again, and it runs through your work now. It will still be carrying when the walls above it come down, and I shall have to look at it every time I come back down here, which I expect to do often. Whatever is back there goes on sleeping. I have decided that is the outcome I wanted, and I will be saying so as though I said it first.

options.text: You did say it first.
Let's get back up into the light.

fork_reward_done._comment: A seal_opened arm for the same hatch Olesm's posted node carries: a player who broke the seal first and re-cut the ward after is describing a repair, not an untouched pour. hide_when is FORBIDDEN -- it would close the hatch.

text_variants.text: There. It runs again, and the work it runs through this time is yours. It will be down here long after the walls are, and I shall have to keep coming back to look at it. The door behind it stays open, so this is a repair. I had a better word ready and the facts declined it. I have decided that is the outcome I wanted, and I will be saying so as though I said it first.

the_appetite._comment: The MINIMUM read, deliberately plainer than the [Detect Magic] arm's quartet payoff -- the literate player gets the lattice, everyone gets the fact.
the_appetite.speaker: Pisces
the_appetite.text: This was not cut as a lock; the hand that made it was too generous for that. The lines run one way, they have run one way for a very long time, and that makes this a feeding ward. Something behind that stone has been drinking since before there were walls up there.

options.text: Feeding what?
Back to you, then.

the_appetite_unknown.speaker: Pisces
the_appetite_unknown.text: I do not know. That is the problem, and I want it written down that I said so first. A ward this careful was not built to imprison. It was built to keep something, the way you keep a fire, and someone chose to keep it fed rather than let it go out.

options.text: Then we decide what to do about it.
I need to think.
